title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board met Tuesday evening and breezed through their light agenda and welcomed a new trustee to the board, following the passing of former member R.C. Franklin Jr., who served as trustee at least since 2017.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order and with no members of the public on hand to speak, the mayor moved forward.  He asked if any trustee had a question about the past meeting minutes or the bills.  Trustee Beth Prosser, who was attending remotely, had a question about the billing for Village Attorney Barry Bright’s services.  Since he was absent due to illness, Prosser withdrew her comment and a motion was made to approve the minutes and the bills and after a second the measure was approved unanimously.

The mayor then moved to an issue the board has struggled with for the past two meetings.  Namely, whether to purchase or lease a new backhoe or to purchase the leased backhoe they have now.  Delonshaw presented information that shows a new backhoe would cost over $100,000 and a used one could cost less, but you can’t be sure what kind of history it has.  The mayor said he believes the best option is to buy their leased backhoe.  He pledged to try to purchase an extended warranty if possible.  The board agreed and approved the purchase of their 2021 John Deere Backhoe for $52,420 with no dissent.

Mayor Delonshaw said with the passing of longtime Trustee R.C. Franklin, he had been contacted by Mike Shock who requested that he be appointed to serve the remainder of Franklin’s term.  A brief discussion ensued amongst members of the board and with no objections, Shock was approved as a new member.  Shock was not in attendance; however a quick phone call was placed and he arrived a few minutes later.

Next, in Attorney Barry Bright’s absence, the board turned to another carryover issue from the last meeting.  Danielle Lister is seeking to put a house on lot 46 in the Sunset Acres subdivision.  A motion was made to approve an ordinance concerning the sale/purchase agreement authorizing the sale of village-owned real estate.  Trustees approved the ordinance as presented.

Mike Shock arrived and Mayor Delonshaw welcomed him and swore him in as a new trustee and he took a seat and listened as the meeting continued.

The mayor brought up the fees charged for new gas service customers.  Utilities Superintendent Sean Sullens contacted other communities about what they charged for new utility hookups.  After a few comments, it was informally decided the village will charge $700 each for gas, water and sewer with the fees to be officially adopted at the next meeting in October.

Village Clerk Shannon Hall asked the board to approve the trick or treat night for Halloween.  By consensus members approved her suggestion of Thursday, October 29 from 6-8pm.  Hall also stated that Clay City’s application for the OSLAD Grant has been submitted to the state through SCIRP-DC in Salem.  She also noted the village had printed 60 cookbooks for Clay City Civics and used a ream of paper in the process.  She asked the board whether to charge them some $45 or to consider it as a gift.  Board consensus was to not charge them.  The Civics group also asked the village to provide the porta potties during the festival and there was no objection.  She also noted the Clay City Fall Festival with be October 2-4 primarily on Main St.  Hall closed her report by noting the October meeting will be moved to Tuesday, October 13.

With all business complete, Trustee Mike Shock made a motion and the meeting adjourned.

title: SHADOWS OF ELMWOOD
full_story:
Flora Rotary will be hosting its 12th annual Shadows of Elmwood Cemetery Tour on Friday, September 11th and Saturday, September 12th. Tickets will be available at the Flora Depot.

Ticket sales will start just before 5 pm with the first wagon leaving at 5 each night.  Tickets are sold until 9 pm and the wagons will go until the last patron has gone through.  Tickets are $8 each unless you purchase a Benefactor Ticket at $25 and go to the front of the line to get on the next available wagon.

The club will also have ride assist tickets for those unable to ride on the hay wagons.  If you are physically unable to ride the wagon, they will have spots available on golf carts that will follow the wagons through the cemetery.  Tickets are reserved for those who are in need, and available on a first come first served basis.

While you wait at the Depot there will be 2 additional skits to keep you entertained and there will be concessions available from Krazy Sweet Treats.

All proceeds from the cemetery tour go to Flora Rotary for their projects in the community.  The Rotary Club is currently working on updating Flora Rotary Park and adding improvements at Flora’s Pickleball Courts.

Jessica Muskopf is today’s guest on The ReVue to talk about this Years Shadows of Elmwood.

title: SHOOTING VIDEO RELEASED
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) released video of a a shooting incident that occurred in July in an Effingham Church.  The Effingham Police Department and the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office requested the Illinois State Police (ISP) Division of Criminal Investigation Zone 8 to investigate a shooting incident at St. John’s Lutheran Church.

On July 5th at approximately 9:27 am, St. John’s Lutheran Church security contacted the Effingham Police Department to report a suspicious vehicle and suspicious man inside the church wishing to speak with the pastor.  The Effingham Police Department and the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office responded to the church locating the man, 36-year-old Allen O. Gattino of St. Charles, MO.  The suspicious vehicle was reported stolen out of Marion County.  Officers from both agencies attempted to restrain Gattino.  During the struggle, Gattino produced a firearm, which discharged, and Gattino was struck.  Gattino was taken to a local hospital and later transported by helicopter to a regional hospital with life-threatening injuries, where he was pronounced deceased.  No one else was injured in this incident.

In accordance with ISP’s commitment to integrity and public transparency, the video of the shooting is being made available to the public and can be found by clicking HERE.  ISP provided Gattino’s family the opportunity to review the video before it was released to the public.

Upon completion of the investigation, ISP submitted the case to the Effingham County State’s Attorney’s Office.

title: EFFINGHAM MAN SENTENCED
full_story:
An Effingham resident was sentenced to prison for robbery and burglary.

Nicholas Courtright, 21, was sentenced to 10 years on a charge of aggravated robbery a class 1 felony.  The sentence stemmed from the March 31st incident at Days Inn.

Effingham city police reported that a man armed with a knife had demanded the motel’s cash drawer from an employee.  After seizing the cash drawer, the subject fled the scene.  A drone and a K9 led to finding Courtright in a makeshift encampment in a wooded area behind Boos Outlet Showroom, where he was taken into custody.

A Class X count of armed robbery was dismissed as part of the negotiated plea.  Courtright was also sentenced to four years in prison for burglary a class X felony.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
In its latest crop progress and condition report released Aug. 31, USDA estimated 11% of Illinois corn was mature, with the same percentage of soybeans dropping leaves.  High temperatures across much of the state this week are expected to accelerate maturity and help dry down crops.

There were 6.3 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending August 30th.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 3% very short, 17% short, 73% adequate, and 7% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 20% short, 71% adequate, and 4% surplus.

Corn dough reached 94%, compared to the 5-year average of 90%.  Corn dented reached 62%, compared to the 5-year average of 63%.  Corn mature reached 11% even with the 5-year average.  Corn condition was rated 4% very poor, 8% poor, 30% fair, 46% good, and 12% excellent.

Soybeans setting pods 94%, compared to the 5-year average of 92%.  Soybeans dropping leaves reached 11%, compared to the 5-year average of 7%.  Soybeans condition was rated 5% very poor, 7% poor, 29% fair, 46% good, and 13% excellent.
